title: Deduction and induction: the difference
coreMove: Choose the reasoning motion the material can honestly carry: linked chain for deduction, parallel pattern for induction.
sourcePressure: Chapter 5 distinguishes deduction and induction, how each works, when to use each, and how inductive reasoning differs inside pyramid logic.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using deduction and induction as impressive labels while mixing chain logic and sibling logic in the same support set.

sourceAnchors.name: deduction and induction
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar lists Deduction and induction: the difference, How it works, When to use it, Inductive reasoning, and How it differs
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The writer has to know whether the reader is following a chain or recognizing a pattern among siblings.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective recognition, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm through a direct second-person passage, a short research/source aside, a reader question, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a tax policy analyst explaining why a rebate will miss renters
exampleSpecs.stakes: lawmakers may support a measure that helps the wrong households if the chain is flattened
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily draws the statutory eligibility chain step by step and refuses to present it as three independent concerns.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A highlighter rests across a marked-up rebate statute.

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant group comparing three reasons to close one underperforming location
exampleSpecs.audience: operators writing board notes with parallel reasons
exampleSpecs.stakes: the closure case weakens if independent reasons are forced into a causal staircase
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Labor did not cause the lease, and the lease did not cause foot traffic," Nicolas says, then turns a fake chain into an inductive group.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Labor did not cause the lease," Nicolas says above the profit-and-loss binder.

exampleSpecs.domain: a wildlife refuge manager explaining an invasive-plant spread
exampleSpecs.stakes: the wrong intervention gets chosen if seed dispersal, mowing, and wetland access are listed as parallel issues
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace asks whether the items are siblings, then traces the actual chain from mowing schedule to seed spread to blocked wetland access.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Why did the reed grass appear first along the service road?

exampleSpecs.domain: an insurance claims trainer writing denial guidance
exampleSpecs.audience: trainers who must show rule application cleanly
exampleSpecs.stakes: new adjusters will deny claims incorrectly if legal conditions and examples are mixed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pavel separates the deductive rule path from inductive examples, then writes two different support sections instead of one confused one.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Pavel one appealed claim to see his training page had two motions.
mustAvoid: marine insurer storm claims from ch3

exampleSpecs.domain: a ballet company production manager justifying a rehearsal change
exampleSpecs.audience: arts administrators balancing physical constraints and schedule reasons
exampleSpecs.stakes: dancers may reject the change if a real injury-prevention chain is presented as a preference list
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Laura show how floor fatigue leads to technique drift and then to injury risk, preserving the deductive chain instead of flattening it.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can hear resin crackle under slippers at the edge of the sprung floor.

exampleSpecs.domain: a renewable-energy procurement lead summarizing supplier risks
exampleSpecs.audience: procurement teams comparing parallel risk categories
exampleSpecs.stakes: contract choice changes if shipping, warranty, and inverter compatibility stay as comparable siblings
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 3:35 p.m., Tomás removes causal arrows between unrelated supplier risks and creates an inductive summary that names their shared effect on delivery certainty.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 3:35 p.m., Tomás erases three arrows from the supplier-risk board.

skillTargets: recognize when support is a chain versus a sibling set
avoid forcing independent reasons into a fake sequence
avoid flattening causal progression into bullets
repair a section that switches reasoning motion midstream

tryThisNowSpec: Mark one support set with C for chain step or S for sibling reason. If both marks appear in one group, split the section before writing the conclusion.
